question: Which of the following events occurs when insulin binds to its receptor ?:

options.opa: Increases the amount of phosphorylated threonine residues in the sub subunits of the receptor.
options.opb: Increases the amount of phosphorylated serine and threonine residues in the extracellular part of the receptor.
options.opc: The receptor catalyzes its own phosphorylation on tyrosine residues from its cytosolic part.
options.opd: The receptor is autophosphorylated in the extracellular region where its ɑ and β chains are contacted.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "binds to its receptor" -> "activates the receptor" -> "triggers autophosphorylation" -> "on tyrosine residues" -> 80% CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "interacts with its receptor" -> "induces phosphorylation" -> "on tyrosine residues" -> 75% CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "attaches to its receptor" -> "promotes autophosphorylation" -> "on tyrosine residues" -> 80%
enhanced_information: When insulin binds to its receptor, the receptor catalyzes its own phosphorylation on tyrosine residues from its cytosolic part. This is supported by the consensus that insulin binding activates the receptor, triggering autophosphorylation specifically on tyrosine residues. The evidence path showing interaction with T-lymphocyte receptors aligns with this process.
analysis: Insulin binding to its receptor triggers the receptor to catalyze its own phosphorylation on tyrosine residues from its cytosolic part. This process of autophosphorylation is a key step in the activation of the receptor.
